The Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender, on 4
October, 2024
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

entities.text: Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.497 of 2013
Judgment:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant and Sri A.Krupadhar Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer, Ramagundam, aggrieved by the order and decree dated 12.03.2013 passed in O.P.No.39 of 2012 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Peddapalli (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court').
3.

In brief, the facts of the case are that the subject lands admeasuring Acs.23.16 guntas situated in the limits of Peddapalli Village and Mandal, Karimanagar District, belonging to the respondents/claimants were acquired for laying of Pipe line under Moulana Abdul Kalam Hyderabad Sujala Sravanthi Project; that the Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published 2 AKS, J & LNA, J in the A.P. Gazette on 24.04.2010; that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act and after conducting enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award, dated 02.09.2011, fixing market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.1,15,000/- per acre.
4.

Not being satisfied with the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was referred to the competent civil Court and was numbered as O.P.No.39 of 2012 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/ claimants, P.Ws-1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-6 were marked.
On behalf of the Referring Officer, RW-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. The Reference Court, on appreciation of the evidence, enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,15,000/- per acre to Rs.7,00,000/- per acre for the acquired lands and further, enhanced the compensation for the acquired wells and trees by one time over and above the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, apart from granting all other benefits under the Act to the 3 The Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender, on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8909241/
1 AKS, J & LNA, J respondents/claimants.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Challenging the said order, the present appeal is filed.

7. It is contended by the learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant that the Reference Court failed to take note of the fact that the Land Acquisition Officer has adopted the sale deeds for three years preceding the date of 4(1) notification for fixing the market value of the acquired lands; that the Reference Court erred in placing reliance on Exs.A-1 to A-5- registered sale deeds, which pertain to lands situated far away from the acquired lands while determining the market value of the acquired lands; that the Reference Court erred in observing that the acquired lands are in residential locality and fetches higher compensation; that the Reference Court erred in enhancing the compensation for the wells and trees existing in the subject acquired lands without considering the fact that the Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation for the same based on the estimates made by the Executive Engineer; and as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.
4 AKS, J & LNA, J 8.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants contended that the Reference Court has rightly appreciated the evidence available on record and on finding that the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer does not commensurate to the potentiality of the subject acquired lands, and by taking into consideration the sale transactions under Exs.A-1 to A-5, rightly enhanced the market value of the acquired lands and therefore, the impugned order needs no interference by this Court.
9. Before the Reference Court, to prove their claim for enhancement, the respondents-claimants have got marked Exs.A-1 to A-5-sale deeds.
10. Ex.A-1 is sale deed dated 28.01.2010, under which land was sold @ Rs.10,02,667/- per acre.
11. Ex.A-2 is sale deed dated 03.03.2010, under which land was sold @ Rs.10,00,000/- per acre.
12. Ex.A-3 is sale deed dated 17.10.2008, under which land was sold @ Rs.72,61,015/- per acre.
5 AKS, J & LNA, J 13.
Ex .A-4 is sale deed dated 17.10.2008, under which land was sold @ Rs.72,62,750/- per acre.
14. Ex.A-5 is sale deed dated 24.12.2008, under which land was sold @ Rs.96,80,000/- per acre.

15. Claimant No.44 got himself examined as P.W-1 and deposed inter alia reiterating that the market value of the acquired lands is more than Rs.20,00,000/- per acre; that the acquired lands are adjacent to Rajiv State Highway; and that the lands covered under Exs.A-1 toA-5 are very near to the acquired lands.

The Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender, on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8909241/
2 16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The attestor of Ex.A-1-sale deed was examined as P.W.2.
He reiterated the contents of Ex.A-1 and further deposed that the land covered under Ex.A-1 and the subject acquired lands are similar in all aspects and fetches the same market value.

Though P.Ws.1 and 2 were cross-examined at length,
their evidence stood unrebutted.
17. P.Ws.1 and 2 in one voice stated that the acquired lands are abutting Rajiv State Highway.

Even R.W-1 admitted that the acquired lands are abutting Rajiv State Highway leading from 6 AKS, J &
LNA, J Ramagundam to Hyderabad.
Even in Ex.B-1-Award, it is stated that the acquired lands are situated in Peddapalli Mandal Headquarters.

Further, it is pertinent to note that in Ex.B-1-Award,
almost all the sale statistics collected and analyzed by the Land Acquisition Officer are regarding sale of lands in bits i.e., for construction of houses, schools, commercial establishments, etc.

As such, the location of the subject acquired lands and their potentiality to be used for house sites,
though they are agricultural lands at the time of acquisition, are well established by the respondents-claimants.

18. Therefore, from the above, it is evident that the respondents- claimants have established that the acquired lands are having high potentiality for house sites as they are abutting Rajiv State Highway and as such, they fetch higher market value.

19. A reading of the impugned order shows that the Reference Court has scrupulously and minutely gone through the sale deeds referred to by the Land Acquisition Officer in Ex.B-1-Award and after analyzing the same, found that the Land Acquisition Officer has rejected almost all the sale transactions of Sulthanabad town on 7 AKS, J & LNA, J the ground that they do not represent the true and real market value for fixation of compensation for the acquired lands and further, the Land Acquisition Officer has followed a pick and choose method while adopting the sale transactions.

20. It is well settled that for fixing the fair and reasonable market value of the subject acquired lands, the factors like its location, extent, potentiality, its use, nearness to the developed area, or whether it is developed land, etc., have to be taken into consideration while appreciating the evidence adduced by the claimants in the form of sale deeds to buttress their claim for enhancement of market value of the subject acquired lands.
21.

In this context, it is also relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Jawajee Nagnatham v. RDO 1 , wherein it is held as under:-
"The burden of proof is always on the claimant to prove the prevailing market value as on the date of notification with reference to the sale deeds of the same lands or neighbouring lands possessed of same or similar advantages and features executed between (1994) 4 SCC 595 8 AKS, J & LNA, J willing vendor and willing vendee or other relevant evidence in the reference court."
22. In the instant case, as observed in the preceding paragraphs, the respondents/claimants have proved their claim as regards the location and potentiality of the subject acquired lands.

The Land Acquisition Officer And ... vs Bonkuri Mahender, on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8909241/
3 23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though Exs.A-2 to A-5-sale deeds were got marked on behalf of the claimants, there is no averment or contention by the claimants that the lands covered under Exs.A-2 to A-5-sale deeds are nearby or in the vicinity of the subject acquired lands and that both are similar in nature or potentiality or features and as such, they fetch same market value.
24. Furthermore, the market value reflected in Exs.A-3 to A-5 is Rs.72,61,015/-, Rs.72,62,250/- and Rs.96,80,000/- per acre.
In the claim petition, the claimants have claimed that the market value of the subject acquired lands as on the date of 4(1) notification was Rs.20,00,000/- per acre.
Claimant No.44 who got himself examined as P.W-1 also deposed that the market value of the subject acquired lands is not less than Rs.20,00,000/- per acre.

Thus, the value reflected in Exs.A-3 to A-5-sale deeds is far high 9 AKS, J & LNA, J and nearly four times more than the market value sought to be fixed by the claimants for the subject acquired lands.

25. Therefore, applying the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Jawajee Nagnatham's case (cited supra) to the facts of the instant case, this Court is of the view that sale deeds under Exs.A-3 to A-5 do not fall in the zone of consideration for fixation of market value of the subject acquired lands and hence, the same cannot be looked into.
26.
As regards the sale deed under Ex.A-1, it is to be seen that the attestor thereto, as mentioned earlier, was examined as P.W-2.
He deposed to the effect that the land covered under Ex.A-1 and the subject acquired lands are similar in nature and fetches the same market value.
The sale consideration reflected under Ex.A-1- sale deed is @ Rs.10,02,667/- per acre.
The evidence of P.W-2 stood unrebutted.

Therefore, it is construed that the sale deed under Ex.A-1 is a bona fide and genuine transaction, which can be taken as a representative sale for fixation of fair and reasonable market value of the subject acquired lands.
10 AKS, J & LNA, J 27.

A perusal of the impugned order shows that the Reference Court has taken Ex.A-1 as exemplar sale deed and fixed the market value of the subject acquired lands based on the said sale transaction,
which, for the reasons assigned by this Court in the foregoing paragraphs, cannot be found fault with.

28. As regards the compensation for the wells and trees existing in the subject acquired lands, it is to be seen that in Ex.A-6- Estimates, the value of the wells is estimated three times more than the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer.

The Reference Court taking a realistic approach and stance has rightly enhanced the compensation for the same by one time above the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, which, in the opinion of this Court sounds reasonable and fair.

29. Hence, having regard to the aforementioned facts and circumstances of the case and for the aforesaid reasons, this Court is of the considered view that the Reference Court has rightly fixed the market value of the subject acquired lands and therefore, this Court finds no justification to interfere with the impugned order passed by the Reference Court.

4 11 AKS, J & LNA, J 30.

sentences.text: Accordingly, this Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
31. As a sequel, interim order dated 04.10.2013 passed in LAASMP.No.1294 of 2013 shall stand vacated.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
